description: A column declared COLLATE 'en-ci' compares equal regardless of case - in WHERE equality and in JOIN ON conditions (qualified and unqualified) - while columns without the collation stay case-sensitive. Converted 1:1 from ddl/CollationCaseInsensitiveTest (now retired).

steps.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ct WHERE s = 'abc'
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ct WHERE s = 'ABC'
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ct WHERE s = 'xyz'
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ct2 WHERE s = 'abc'
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ct2 WHERE s = 'ABC'
CREATE TABLE cfg (module_id VARCHAR COLLATE 'en-ci', qualified VARCHAR)

SELECT COUNT(l.qualified)
FROM stg s LEFT JOIN cfg l ON l.module_id = s.lookup_key
CREATE TABLE cfg3 (module_id VARCHAR COLLATE 'en-ci', v VARCHAR)
SELECT COUNT(l.v) FROM stg3 s INNER JOIN cfg3 l ON module_id = k
